summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with acute myeloid leukemia in remission following double cord blood transplant, was admitted with fevers, rigors, and hypoxic respiratory failure. He was found to have Stenotrophomonas maltophilia bacteremia, likely from his central venous catheter, and was treated with IV antibiotics after line removal. His oxygen requirements improved, and repeat cultures were negative. He developed acute kidney injury, attributed to a benign lab effect from Bactrim, which resolved after discontinuation. An echocardiogram revealed a reduced ejection fraction of 40%, and he was discharged on heart failure medications. An infected ingrown toenail was surgically treated, and he completed a course of oral antibiotics. Mental status changes were evaluated with a normal brain MRI. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned for cardiology, nephrology, pulmonary, podiatry, and ophthalmology.
